lines.name: Motor
lines.fallback: [iFlight XING 2814 880KV](https://shop.iflight.com/xing-x2814-fpv-nextgen-motor-pro838): the same 19 x 19 mm mount and 5 mm shaft, 6 g heavier, and a lower peak; its thrust table is only an image, so the sizing model would need it read first
lines.note: out of stock at EMAX USA on the day; EMAX's global shop had it at $58.50

lines.name: Prop
lines.fallback: [HQProp MacroQuad 10x5x3, 2 CW + 2 CCW](https://www.readymaderc.com/products/details/86878-hq-macroquad-prop-10x5x3-2ccw-2cw-black-glass-fiber-reinforced-nylon): the same size and hub, 6 g a prop heavier, and the motor's thrust table was measured on Gemfan, so recheck
lines.note: two turn each way; sold in pairs at $11.99; back ordered at GetFPV on the day

lines.name: 4-in-1 ESC
lines.fallback: [Lumenier ELITE PRO 60A 2-6S AM32 4-in-1, 30x30](https://www.getfpv.com/electronics/electronic-speed-controllers-esc/4-in-1-esc-s/lumenier-elite-pro-60a-2-6s-am32-4-in-1-esc-30x30.html): the same AM32 firmware and mount with more headroom, but 13 g heavier and 3 mm taller, against the frame's 19 mm stack height

lines.name: Frame
lines.fallback: [GEPRC GEP-Mark4-10 frame kit](https://www.readymaderc.com/products/details/86588-geprc-mark4-10-multirotor-frame): the same stack and motor mounts and 75 g lighter, but a different plate layout, so the CAD needs a new frame
lines.note: the catalog's $115.99 couldn't be found anywhere; iFlight's own shop doesn't list it

lines.name: Cell
lines.fallback: [Molicel INR-21700-P42A](https://imrbatteries.com/products/molicel-p42a-21700-4200mah-45a-battery): the same size and 45 A rating; the pack drops from 9.0 to 8.4 Ah, about 7% less flight time
lines.note: for the 6S2P pack; out of stock at Liion Wholesale on the day; GetFPV had it at about $13 a cell, in stock

lines.name: ARK FPV flight controller
lines.fallback: [Holybro Kakute H7 V1.5 (SKU 11091)](https://holybro.com/products/kakute-h7): the same STM32H743 and mount and runs PX4, but different sensors (my firmware's drivers are written for the ARK's), no compass and solder pads instead of JST-GH
lines.note: in stock on the day; ARK lists its barometer as a BMP390, which my firmware's driver also accepts

lines.name: RP2 V2 ExpressLRS 2.4 GHz receiver
lines.fallback: [BETAFPV ELRS Nano Receiver 2.4GHz](https://racedayquads.com/products/betafpv-elrs-nano-2-4ghz-receiver): the same CRSF wiring, but a T antenna on U.FL to mount
lines.note: order the FCC version

lines.name: TF-Luna lidar
lines.fallback: [Benewake TFmini-S (SparkFun SEN-16977)](https://www.sparkfun.com/tfmini-s-micro-lidar-module.html): longer range (12 m) at the same weight, but a different body for the bracket and a tighter 5 V supply

lines.name: Teensy 4.1 (safety monitor)
lines.fallback: [PJRC (made by SparkFun) Teensy 4.0 (DEV-15583)](https://www.sparkfun.com/teensy-4-0.html): the same chip, but fewer pins, no microSD and a different size: the monitor's pin map and mount change
lines.note: PJRC sends buyers to SparkFun, which makes Teensy now

lines.name: LSM6DSOX 6-DoF accelerometer and gyroscope breakout (product 4438)
lines.fallback: [Adafruit LSM6DSO32 breakout (4692)](https://www.adafruit.com/product/4692): the same family; its accelerometer has no +-2 g range, so the monitor's range setting changes

lines.name: Transmitter
lines.fallback: [RadioMaster Boxer EdgeTX ELRS](https://www.racedayquads.com/products/pre-order-radiomaster-boxer-edgetx-rc-transmitter-choose-version): full-size gimbals and up to 1 W, at two and a half times the price; the switch names change
lines.note: The pilot's sticks and the kill switch, over 2.4 GHz ExpressLRS (the control link stays off 900 MHz). SA arms, SD is the kill switch, both two-position latching. Takes two 18650s, not included

lines.name: HaLow on the laptop's side
lines.fallback: [Morse Micro (with GL.iNet) HaLowLink 2](https://www.gl-inet.com/en-us/products/halowlink2): Morse Micro's own router, about $130 (seen in search results), but a newer MM8108 chip: bench-test it against the drone's MM6108 first
lines.note: The ground end of V's video and telemetry link, over Ethernet to the laptop. The same MM6108 chip as the drone's card. Which card the drone gets is still my call

lines.name: Balance charger
lines.fallback: [HOTA D6 Pro dual channel](https://www.racedayquads.com/products/hota-d6-pro-dual-channel-325w-15a-ac-dc-battery-charger): the same 200 W AC limit, two channels, bulkier
lines.note: Charges the 6S Li-ion pack through its balance lead. On AC it tops out around 6 to 7 A for this pack; a full 8 A needs a 24 V DC supply

lines.name: Smoke stopper
lines.fallback: [JHEMCU XT30 / XT60 Smoke Stopper](https://www.racedayquads.com/products/jhemcu-xt30-xt60-smoke-stopper): a resettable fuse with a 0.5 A hold: only good for the very first power-on
lines.note: An electronic fuse in series for the first power-up, so a wiring mistake trips instead of burning. Use its 2 A setting so the ESC's capacitors don't trip it

lines.name: Nickel-plated copper strip, 10 x 0.3 mm, 2 m
lines.model: Nickel-plated copper strip, 10 mm x 0.3 mm, 2 m
lines.fallback: [Unbranded nickel-plated copper strip, 8 x 0.15 mm, 10 ft](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0B789WW5D): thinner: two or three layers stacked for the same current, or the pack's limit rechecked
lines.note: The pack's cell links: copper carries the 90 A cap at 15 A/mm2, where nickel strip would run at 37. Small spot welders struggle with 0.3 mm copper: check the welder

lines.name: Insulator rings for 21700 cells, 20
lines.model: 21700 battery terminal insulator rings, black, 20 pcs
lines.note: Insulates each cell's positive end from the strip

lines.name: Pack heat shrink
lines.model: PVC heat shrink, 200 mm flat, 3 m
lines.note: The pack's outer wrap; the flat width depends on the cell layout

lines.name: 6S balance lead
lines.model: 6S JST-XH balance lead, 100 mm, 22 AWG silicone
lines.note: The seven wires from the pack's junctions to its JST-XH plug

lines.name: Heat shrink assortment
lines.note: Over every soldered end in the wiring guide, 3 mm to 10 mm

lines.name: Soldering iron, solder and flux
lines.note: A temperature-controlled iron that holds its heat on the ESC's 12 AWG pads, solder and flux

lines.name: Multimeter
lines.model: A digital multimeter with continuity and a low ohms range
lines.note: Every check in the wiring guide and the test plans; one that reads continuity and low resistance

lines.name: Spot welder
lines.model: A battery spot welder that can weld 0.3 mm copper strip
lines.note: The pack's strip goes on by spot welding; cells are never soldered. Not needed if the pack is bought built

lines.name: Prop balancer
lines.model: A magnetic prop balancer for 5 mm bores
lines.note: The arms ring sideways close to what an unbalanced prop shakes them at in a hover (the structure report)

lines.name: Props, a spare set
lines.note: Props break; a set of four, two each way, like the build's (sold in pairs)

lines.name: MINI fuses, spares
lines.model: MINI blade fuses, 297 series, two 3 A and two 2 A
lines.note: The two branch fuses are soldered in; keep spares of both ratings

lines.name: microSD card for the Pi
lines.fallback: SanDisk Extreme 64GB microSDXC A2: the same class; its price couldn't be confirmed on the day
lines.note: The Pi 5 boots from it; Raspberry Pi's own A2 card is the one specified for the Pi 5

lines.name: Carbon tube for the GPS mast
lines.model: Carbon fiber tube, 8 mm outside, at least 100 mm long
lines.note: The mast's tube, 8 mm across and 90 mm tall in the CAD (design/cad.yaml); the printed foot and cradle hold it

lines.name: Release servo (stand-in)
lines.fallback: [Hitec RCD HS-65MG (32065S)](https://hitecrcd.com/hs-65mg-metal-gear-analog-micro-servo/): metal gears and more torque, 4 g heavier; maybe the better release servo
lines.note: The Harrier bundle has no servo. This is the design's stand-in until Fruity Chutes says which one theirs is

open: P in every combination, and an optical flow sensor in Base (step 4's findings): the package builds what's designed today.
The HaLow card: Heltec's SPI card has no working Pi 5 report yet, and its swap waits for me. The ground side's HaLow radio waits with it.
V's camera: its bracket tips it 30 degrees for the live video, too oblique for mapping. A mapping position or a tilt servo is a weight call for me.
The claws (C): a placeholder until the claw conversation.
Fruity Chutes' release servo (Hitec's HS-55 stands in) and the canopy's opening time.
The safety monitor's Teensy image: it needs PJRC's Teensy core, a download for me to approve.
